title: Odile and the Well
premise: Ulyana Coldharbour takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Grayfen, where students vanish from the attendance ledger and no one will say where they go. On their first night, the imaginary friend from Ulyana's childhood—Odile—is waiting on the porch, unchanged after twenty years, and reveals that the Coldharbour family has been paying a tithe to the thing in the old well to stay alive. As the count of missing children accelerates toward a final reckoning, Ulyana must choose between protecting their own kin and exposing the town's complicity. In the end, Ulyana breaks the generational bargain by giving the well what it truly wants—the truth spoken aloud—and seals it at the cost of Odile's existence and their family's home.
about_author: August Villalobos is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in coastal towns where the census never quite matched the graveyards. They write horror about institutions that keep records instead of promises.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives in Grayfen and inherits not just a classroom but a leather attendance ledger with pages torn out. POV: Ulyana. Beat: unease dressed as professional optimism.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Desks
chapters.summary: Ulyana counts twenty-six desks but the roster lists thirty-one names; the janitor, Mr. Pell, warns them not to ask about the difference. POV: Ulyana. Beat: first crack in normalcy.

chapters.title: The Porch Light
chapters.summary: On their first night in the rented Coldharbour cottage, Ulyana finds Odile—a tall, gray figure from childhood—waiting on the porch, unchanged. POV: Ulyana. Beat: terror braided with homesickness.

chapters.title: What Odile Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile speaks only in things Ulyana said as a child, repeating warnings like 'count the doors.' Ulyana dismisses it as stress. POV: Ulyana. Beat: denial.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: A student, Bram Tuller, is absent; his desk is gone by afternoon and no one remembers him but Ulyana. POV: Ulyana. Beat: gaslighting dread.

chapters.title: Aunt Vess's Rules
chapters.summary: Ulyana's aunt Vess, the last Coldharbour in town, visits with groceries and rules: keep lights on, count doors nightly, never answer the well. POV: Ulyana. Beat: warmth laced with menace.

chapters.title: Down the Hill
chapters.summary: Ulyana walks to the old well on Coldharbour land against every rule and hears something counting back. POV: Ulyana. Beat: forbidden curiosity rewarded with horror.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: The principal, Mrs. Harkaway, praises Ulyana for 'not making trouble' about absences; Ulyana notices her own name appearing in an old ledger. POV: Ulyana. Beat: institutional complicity revealed.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile finally speaks new words: the Coldharbours bought survival generations ago, paying children to the well so their line would be spared. POV: Ulyana. Beat: inheritance as curse.

chapters.title: Vess Confesses
chapters.summary: Aunt Vess admits she has kept the payments current since Ulyana's parents' deaths—and that Ulyana was once offered as payment and spared by a substitution. POV: Vess (rare shift). Beat: guilt and love entangled.

chapters.title: The Substituted Child
chapters.summary: Ulyana learns the child who took their place was Odile—once real, now returned as the well's leftover messenger. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief reframes everything.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: Doors in the cottage begin multiplying overnight; Ulyana counts nine where there were five, each slightly open. POV: Ulyana. Beat: domestic space turning hostile.

chapters.title: Bram's Voice
chapters.summary: Bram Tuller's voice calls from the well during class recess; only Ulyana hears it. POV: Ulyana. Beat: moral alarm—the missing are alive down there.

chapters.title: Harkaway's Office
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Mrs. Harkaway, who shows her own family ledger: everyone in Grayfen owes the well someone. POV: Ulyana. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Tithe Schedule
chapters.summary: Vess reveals the schedule: one child per season, and this season's date is days away—with Ulyana's student Wren marked as next. POV: Ulyana. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Ulyana tries to warn twelve-year-old Wren Okafor, who is sharp, unafraid, and already dreaming of the well. POV: alternating Ulyana/Wren. Beat: protective instinct ignites.

chapters.title: Odile Interferes
chapters.summary: Odile blocks Ulyana from going to authorities, insisting interference voids the family's protection. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the guardian becomes the jailer.

chapters.title: The Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Ulyana attends a harvest meeting where the 'school fund' is collected in silence; every parent pays without looking up. POV: Ulyana. Beat: complicity as ritual.

chapters.title: Nine Doors Open
chapters.summary: All nine doors in the cottage stand open at midnight, and something walks through them counting aloud. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the house itself is a mouth.

chapters.title: Vess's Mistake
chapters.summary: Vess misses a payment deadline while tending Ulyana's fever; the well sends a notice—a child's shoe on the porch. POV: Vess. Beat: debt comes due.

chapters.title: Fever Dreams
chapters.summary: Sick, Ulyana dreams the original bargain: their great-grandmother trading a neighbor's child for her own. POV: Ulyana (dream). Beat: inherited sin made visceral.

chapters.title: Wren Disappears
chapters.summary: Wren doesn't come to school; her desk vanishes before lunch. Ulyana breaks protocol and runs to the well. POV: Ulyana. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Well's Mouth
chapters.summary: At the well, Ulyana hears many voices below, including Wren's, singing a counting song. The well offers a trade: a Coldharbour for all of them. POV: Ulyana. Beat: temptation with a terrible price.

chapters.title: Odile's Plea
chapters.summary: Odile begs Ulyana to pay—insisting that if the family falls, everything Odile suffered was for nothing. POV: Ulyana. Beat: loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: Harkaway's Threat
chapters.summary: Mrs. Harkaway threatens to have Ulyana committed, revealing the town has erased troublesome teachers before. POV: Ulyana. Beat: isolation tightens.

chapters.title: Pell's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Janitor Pell, dying, confesses he helped dig the well deeper in 1968 and saw what lives below; he gives Ulyana his old key. POV: Pell. Beat: a reluctant ally.

chapters.title: The Key
chapters.summary: The key opens a bricked door beneath the school—the original well-house, older than the town charter. POV: Ulyana. Beat: discovery beneath the institution.

chapters.title: Names on the Bricks
chapters.summary: Inside, every brick bears a child's name scratched from within. Ulyana finds Bram's fresh scratches. POV: Ulyana. Beat: hope that the taken can be reached.

chapters.title: Vess Stands Guard
chapters.summary: Vess catches Ulyana at the well-house and physically blocks the way, choosing the bargain over the children. POV: alternating. Beat: family loyalty curdles into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Zero
chapters.summary: The well begins its final count; doors across town slam open in sequence. The reckoning is ahead of schedule because of Ulyana's interference. POV: Ulyana. Beat: consequences cascade.

chapters.title: Odile's Truth
chapters.summary: Odile confesses the well sent them back not to protect Ulyana but to collect; yet over the weeks, Odile chose Ulyana instead. POV: Odile. Beat: the imaginary friend becomes real through choice.

chapters.title: What the Well Wants
chapters.summary: Ulyana realizes the well doesn't feed on children—it feeds on secrets; the tithes were bribes to keep the town's founding crime buried. POV: Ulyana. Beat: revelation reorients the conflict.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Pell get Wren and two other surviving taken children out through the brick door as the count nears zero. POV: Ulyana. Beat: desperate rescue under countdown.

chapters.title: Vess's Choice
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Vess turns back to hold the door, finally paying her own debt rather than another child's. POV: Vess. Beat: redemption at cost.

chapters.title: The Speaking
chapters.summary: Ulyana stands at the well's mouth and speaks the founding crime aloud—the stolen child, the buried bodies, every name—to a gathering town forced to listen. POV: Ulyana. Beat: climax; truth as exorcism.

chapters.title: The Well Answers
chapters.summary: The well screams through every open door in Grayfen as its hoard of secrets loses power; the ground drinks itself dry. POV: Ulyana. Beat: cathartic destruction.

chapters.title: Goodbye, Odile
chapters.summary: With the bargain broken, Odile fades—but chooses to spend the last hour being remembered properly, named aloud for the first time in decades. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief transfigured into witness.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the missing are mourned publicly, desks return to the classroom, and the ledger is burned. Ulyana stays to teach the survivors. POV: Ulyana. Beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: The Dry Well
chapters.summary: Ulyana fills the well with stones from the ruined schoolhouse foundation, one stone per name read aloud. POV: Ulyana. Beat: ritual closure.

chapters.title: Counting Forward
chapters.summary: On the last day of term, Ulyana counts the doors—one, and it stays one—and leaves the porch light off for the first time. Somewhere far off, a child laughs, and it is only a child. POV: Ulyana. Beat: survival without price, at last.
